1.​ Definition

            ●​ Wolf ribs helmets are bascinet-based helmets topped by a central-pivot facial grill. The
               few available sources are paintings from the Czech Republic and Germany. The
               primary sources are dated from 1380 and 1450.
            ●​ The helmet is very similar to other bascinets. It is constructed with a center-hinge visor
               (such as Klappvisor), locked with a “spoon”, and is worn with an aventail.
            ●​ Wolf ribs helmets are approved for 14th-century and transitional armor.
            ●​ Wolf ribs helmets with bascinet shape are denied for 15th century armors.

3.​ Requirements
         3.1 General Requirements
            ●​ Reproductions must closely resemble the appearance and proportions of the sources.
            ●​ Any metal part of the helmet must conform to the Armors and weapons Aesthetics and
               decorations document.
            ●​ Any textile or leather part of the helmet must conform to the Textiles and Leather
               document.

         3.2 Visor Requirements
            ●​ The visor must not be too long or too short and respect the proportions of historical
               sources.
            ●​ The hinge must be reproduced as per historical sources.
            ●​ It is permitted to weld the hinge. Welded hinges must resemble a functional hinge.
            ●​ It is permitted to weld the visor down. A welded visor must resemble a functional
               removable visor.
            ●​ It is permitted to add a metal plate to protect the throat. Such a plate must be strong
               enough to endure full contact fight and must be concealed under the aventail.
            ●​ The visor must consist of 5 horizontal ribs.
            ●​ Ribs must be round or bar-shaped.
            ●​ Ribs can not be made of flat sheets.

         3.3 Eye-slots
            ●​ It is not recommended to have oversized eye slots (over 30x50mm).
            ●​ It is permitted to add up to four (4) vertical safety eyebars on the visor: two (2) on each
               side of the visor.
            ●​ Eyebars must conform to the Eye Bars rules document.

         3.4 Aventail
            ●​ Wolf ribs helmets can be worn with chainmail or fabric aventails. Scale aventails are
               not permitted.
            ●​ Aventails must conform to the Aventails document.
            ●​ The aventail must be fastened down to the outer edge of a padded pelerine attached to
               the helmet liner.
            ●​ Protective plates covering the cervical spine should be hidden under the aventail.
               Supplemental hidden collar plates are permitted.

         3.5 Others
            ●​ Wolf ribs helmets may be decorated in the spirit of medieval styles, such as an orle,
               torse, decorated aventails (with copper/brass chainmail rings), vervelle covers, coat of
               arms badges, etc.
            ●​ Such decoration must be made in coherence with historical sources.
            ●​ Using modern and/or offensive imagery and slogans is prohibited.
